items.stem: Under IAS 2, inventory is measured at:

options.text: The lower of cost and net realisable value
options.rationale: Correct: IAS 2 requires the lower of cost and NRV.

options.text: Always historical cost, never written down
options.rationale: Write-downs to NRV are required when NRV falls below cost.

options.text: Current replacement cost in all cases
options.rationale: Replacement cost is not the IAS 2 measurement base for finished goods.

options.text: Expected selling price with no deductions
options.rationale: NRV deducts costs to complete and sell.

items.explanation: Correct: IAS 2 requires the lower of cost and NRV.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO signals most strongly suggest inventory should be written down? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Selling price has fallen below cost plus costs to sell
options.rationale: Correct: NRV below cost triggers a write-down.

options.text: A product line has not sold for 18 months with no future demand
options.rationale: Correct: obsolete stock with no realisable value needs writing down.
Faster turnover is positive and does not imply a write-down.
Higher input cost alone does not require a write-down.

items.explanation: Correct: NRV below cost triggers a write-down.

items.stem: In a period of rising prices, FIFO compared with weighted average will generally report:

options.text: Higher closing inventory and higher profit
options.rationale: Correct: FIFO leaves newer, higher-cost items in stock, raising reported profit.

options.text: Lower closing inventory and lower profit
options.rationale: That is the opposite of FIFO's effect in rising prices.
The methods diverge when prices change.

options.text: No inventory on the balance sheet
options.rationale: Both methods still report closing inventory.

items.explanation: Correct: FIFO leaves newer, higher-cost items in stock, raising reported profit.
